title: Holy Roman Empire
question: Is there a Holy Roman Empire covering the German lands?
hint: Central Europe. After August 1806, maps show the Confederation of the Rhine, Austria and Prussia instead.

sources.says: On 6 August 1806, Emperor Francis II abdicated and formally dissolved the empire following the creation by French emperor Napoleon of the Confederation of the Rhine
The Holy Roman Empire was dissolved on the 6th of August in 1806, when the last Holy Roman Emperor, Francis II ... abdicated his title
Francis II, Holy Roman Emperor, who had already proclaimed himself Emperor of Austria in 1804, declared the Holy Roman Empire dissolved

notes: Yes: 1805 or earlier.' Real end is 6 August 1806, so maps from 1805 to mid-1806 can still show it.

title: Republic of Texas
question: Is Texas shown as an independent country (the Republic of Texas)?
hint: Between Mexico and the United States. Before 1836 it is part of Mexico, and after 1845 it is a US state.

sources.says: The Republic of Texas ... was a short-lived sovereign country in North America from March 2, 1836, to February 19, 1846.

The Texas annexation was the incorporation of the Republic of Texas into the United States by joint resolution of Congress, culminating in its admission to the Union as the 28th state on December 29, 1845.
Although Texas was annexed by the United States in late December 1845, the formal transfer ceremony occurred on February 19, 1846

notes: The independence declaration was 2 March 1836. The end uses legal admission to the Union (29 December 1845); the formal handover of power was 19 February 1846.

title: Texas joins the United States
question: Is Texas part of the United States?
hint: The big state on the Gulf of Mexico. Earlier maps show it as Mexican territory or the independent Republic of Texas.

sources.says: The bill was signed by President Polk on December 29, 1845, accepting Texas as the 28th state of the Union.
Tyler managed to get the joint resolution passed on March 1, 1845, and Texas was admitted into the United States on December 29.

notes: Transfer of power took place on 19 February 1846. The third answer, 'part of Mexico', is just the time before both Texas events, so it has no event of its own.

title: Florida becomes American
question: Is the Florida peninsula part of the United States?
hint: Southeastern US. Before 1821, maps show Spanish East and West Florida.

sources.says: This proposal was defeated and the treaty officially made effective on February 22, 1821.
Under the Onís-Adams Treaty of 1819 (also called the Transcontinental Treaty and ratified in 1821) the United States and Spain defined the western limits of the Louisiana Purchase
The Adams–Onís Treaty was signed between the United States and Spain on February 22, 1819, and took effect on July 17, 1821.
On July 10, 1821, the province of East Florida was transferred to Governor Andrew Jackson

notes: The US occupied it in 1818 during the Seminole War, but the treaty was signed in 1819 and only took effect on 22 February 1821, with the formal handovers in July 1821. The US took parts of West Florida (the coast west of the Perdido) piecemeal in 1810-1813. Merged duplicates disagreed on dates: 1821-02..null vs 1821-07..null.

title: Paraguay independent
question: Is there a country called Paraguay?
hint: Landlocked, between Argentina, Brazil and Bolivia. Before 1811 it is part of Spain's Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata.

sources.says: Paraguay overthrew the local Spanish administration on 14 May 1811.
The United States recognized the Republic of Paraguay as a separate and independent state on April 27, 1852
The Independence of Paraguay de facto started on 14 May 1811 after the Revolution of May 14 when a local ruling junta was created.

notes: Paraguay dates its independence to May 1811; it formally declared independence in 1842 and the US recognised it in 1852.

title: Venezuela and Ecuador leave Gran Colombia
question: Are Venezuela and Ecuador shown as separate countries, not part of Colombia?
hint: Northern South America. From 1819 to 1830, maps show one big Colombia (Gran Colombia) that includes both.

sources.says: On 13 May 1830, the Southern District declared its independence from Colombia, forming the State of Ecuador.
Ecuador withdrew from the Colombian federation in 1830
After Venezuela separated from Colombia in 1830, the United States recognized and established diplomatic relations with Venezuela in 1835.
Venezuela remained part of Gran Colombia until 1830, when a rebellion led by José Antonio Páez allowed the proclamation of a newly independent Venezuela, on 22 September
After Ecuador's separation from Colombia on 13 May 1830, its first President, General Juan José Flores, laid claim to the territory...

notes: Gran Colombia was formally abolished in 1831. Before 1819 'Venezuela' can appear as a Spanish captaincy-general label (and as the short-lived First Republic of 1811-12), so the question asks about separate countries. Merged duplicates disagreed on dates: 1830-05..null vs 1830-09..null.

title: Russia reaches the Sea of Japan
question: Does Russia reach the Sea of Japan, with the coast around Vladivostok shown as Russian?
hint: The coast north of Korea. Before 1860 this coast is Chinese (Manchuria).

sources.says: The result was the Russo-Chinese Convention of Peking, which took place on 14 November 1860 ... its terms stipulated that all land north of the Amur and east of the Ussuri would be ceded to Russia.
The territory bounded on the west by the Ussuri, on the north by the Amur, and on the east and south by the Sea of Japan was to be jointly administered by Russia and China
The treaty also confirmed the cession of the entirety of what is now known as Outer Manchuria to the Russian Empire ... sealing off Chinese access to the Sea of Japan.

notes: That treaty only made the Ussuri-to-sea coast a joint Russo-Chinese condominium. Russia got the coast outright in the Sino-Russian Convention of Peking, 14 November 1860.

title: Gadsden Purchase gives the modern US-Mexico border
question: Does the US-Mexico border west of El Paso run in straight lines well south of the Gila River, as it does today?
hint: Southern Arizona and New Mexico. From 1848 to 1854 the border follows the Gila River and southern Arizona is Mexican.

sources.says: The treaty took effect on June 8, 1854.
The Gadsden Purchase, or Treaty, was an agreement between the United States and Mexico, finalized in 1854

notes: This matches the Gadsden Purchase, which took effect on 8 June 1854.

title: Dominion of Canada
question: Is there a Dominion of Canada that includes Nova Scotia and New Brunswick?
hint: Eastern North America. Before July 1867, 'Canada' is only the province along the St Lawrence and Great Lakes; the Maritimes are separate colonies.

sources.says: ...were united into one federation, called the Dominion of Canada, on July 1, 1867.
The United States recognized Canada as an independent state with autonomous control over its foreign relations on February 18, 1927

notes: Confederation (1 July 1867) created the Dominion, but Canada only became fully autonomous in 1926-1931. The US State Department dates its recognition of Canadian independence to 1927.

title: Alaska becomes American
question: Is Alaska shown as part of the United States?
hint: Northwest corner of North America. Before 1867, maps show Russian America.

sources.says: On April 9 of that year, the United States Senate ratified a bilateral treaty that had been signed on March 30, and American sovereignty became legally effective across the territory on October 18.
on March 30, 1867, agreed to a proposal from Russian Minister in Washington, Edouard de Stoeckl, to purchase Alaska for $7.2 million.

notes: Formally it was the Department of Alaska (1867), then the District (1884), then the Territory (1912), then a state (1959).

title: Edo becomes Tokyo
question: Is Japan's capital labelled Tokyo?
hint: Kantō plain, eastern Honshu. Before 1868 maps say Edo (Yedo, Jeddo) and put the imperial capital at Kyoto (Miyako).

sources.says: After being handed over to the Meiji government, Edo was renamed Tokyo (Eastern Capital) on September 3, 1868
Following the overthrow of the Tokugawa shogunate in 1868, the city formerly known as Edo was renamed Tōkyō ("Eastern Capital"), and the emperor’s residence was moved there from Kyoto

notes: Usually dated 3 September 1868 (imperial rescript); the month was not confirmed in an opened source. Merged duplicates disagreed on dates: 1868-09..null vs 1868..null.

title: Union of South Africa
question: Is there a single country called (the Union of) South Africa covering the Cape, Natal, Transvaal and Orange Free State?
hint: Southern tip of Africa. Before May 1910 maps show four separate colonies.

sources.says: It came into existence on 31 May 1910 with the unification of the Cape, Natal, Transvaal, and Orange River colonies.
The Republic of South Africa Constitution Bill ... came into force on 31 May 1961.

notes: Became the Republic of South Africa on 31 May 1961; the map label stays 'South Africa'.

title: Rhodesia on the map
question: Is there a territory labelled Rhodesia (Northern Rhodesia, Southern Rhodesia or just Rhodesia)?
hint: Today's Zambia and Zimbabwe. Before 1895 the area appears as Zambesia, Mashonaland or Matabeleland; after 1980 only Zambia and Zimbabwe remain.

sources.says: The BSAC officially adopted the name "Rhodesia" in May 1895, and the British government followed in 1898.
The Company officially adopted the name Rhodesia in 1895, and three years later the UK government followed suit.
The United States recognized the Republic of Zimbabwe on April 18, 1980
A short-lived sovereign state that existed from 1 June 1979 to 18 April 1980.

notes: The British South Africa Company adopted the name in May 1895. Northern Rhodesia became Zambia in October 1964. Southern Rhodesia was called Rhodesia (1964-79), then Zimbabwe Rhodesia (June-December 1979), then Southern Rhodesia again, and became Zimbabwe on 18 April 1980. Merged duplicates disagreed on dates: 1895-05..1980-04 vs 1895..1980-04.

title: Bolivia loses its coast
question: Is Bolivia landlocked, with Chile holding the coast around Antofagasta?
hint: The Pacific coast of South America around the Tropic of Capricorn. Before the War of the Pacific, Bolivia's Litoral province reaches the sea between Peru and Chile.

sources.says: The Treaty of Ancón ended the conflict between Peru and Chile on 20 October 1883, and a truce was signed by Bolivia and Chile at Valparaíso on 4 April 1884.
Bolivia signed a truce with Chile in 1884.
the Bolivian coast in the Atacama Desert included in the country's territory from its inception in 1825 until 1879, when it was lost to Chile.
Signed on April 4, 1884, the third treaty of the war forced Bolivia to give Antofagasta to Chile.

notes: Under the truce Chile administered the Bolivian coast. Chile had occupied it in 1879. The coast was formally ceded by the 1904 treaty.

title: Buda and Pest merge into Budapest
question: Is the Hungarian capital labelled Budapest, rather than separate Buda and Pest?
hint: On the Danube in Hungary. Before November 1873, maps show Buda (Ofen) and Pest (Pesth) as two towns.

sources.says: The city of Budapest was officially created on 17 November 1873 from a merger of the three neighboring cities of Pest, Buda and Óbuda.
The previously separate cities of Buda, Óbuda, and Pest were officially unified in 1873 and given the new name Budapest.

title: Union of Sweden and Norway
question: Are Sweden and Norway shown joined as one union (Sweden-Norway)?
hint: Scandinavia. Before 1814 Norway goes with Denmark; after 1905 Norway is shown on its own.

sources.says: The fundamental documents were only the Convention of Moss and the revised Norwegian constitution of 4 November 1814.
...negotiations between the two governments led to Sweden's recognition of Norway as an independent constitutional monarchy on 26 October 1905.
Norway’s national assembly (Storting) declared an end to the union with Sweden on June 7, 1905. ... a treaty of separation was signed on October 26, 1905.

notes: Strictly it was a personal union of two kingdoms, though maps often coloured them together. The end date is Sweden's recognition on 26 October 1905; Norway counts the union as ending with the Storting resolution of 7 June 1905.

title: Austria-Hungary
question: Is there a country called Austria-Hungary?
hint: Central Europe around Vienna and Budapest. Before 1867 the area is labelled the Austrian Empire; after 1918 it breaks into Austria, Hungary, Czechoslovakia and others.

sources.says: Infobox: 1867 Compromise, 30 March 1867; Empire dissolved, 31 October 1918.
Franz Joseph and Deák signed the Compromise, and it was ratified by the restored Diet of Hungary on 29 May 1867.
One of Károlyi's first acts was to repudiate the compromise agreement on 31 October, thus officially dissolving the Austro-Hungarian monarchy and state

notes: The start uses the infobox date (30 March 1867); the Hungarian Diet ratified the Compromise on 29 May 1867. The end uses dissolution on 31 October 1918.

title: Albania independent
question: Is there a country called Albania?
hint: On the Adriatic, north of Greece. Before 1912 the area is part of the Ottoman Empire (Turkey in Europe).

sources.says: Independent Albania was proclaimed in Vlorë on 28 November 1912.

notes: Independence was declared on 28 November 1912, so late-1912 maps may already show it. Italy occupied Albania from 1939 to 1943, but maps kept the Albania label.

title: Petrograd renamed Leningrad
question: Is the city at the head of the Gulf of Finland labelled Leningrad?
hint: The eastern end of the Baltic. Before 1924 it is Petrograd (Saint Petersburg until 1914), and from 1991 Saint Petersburg again.

sources.says: On 26 January 1924, shortly after the death of Vladimir Lenin, it was renamed to Leningrad

notes: The city was renamed back to Saint Petersburg on 6 September 1991, after a referendum held that June.

title: Ottoman Empire
question: Is the Ottoman Empire shown (labelled Ottoman Empire or Turkish Empire)?
hint: Centred on Anatolia and Constantinople; before WWI it also holds the Levant, Iraq and parts of Arabia. After 1922 maps show the Republic of Turkey.

sources.says: The sultanate was abolished on 1 November 1922, and the last sultan, Mehmed VI (reigned 1918–1922), left the country on 17 November 1922.
The Grand National Assembly of Turkey abolished the monarchy on 1 November 1922 and ended the Ottoman Empire

notes: English maps often labelled it 'Turkey', so the question also accepts 'Turkish Empire'.

title: Soviet Union
question: Is there a country called the Soviet Union (USSR)?
hint: Spanning northern Eurasia. Before 1922, maps show Russia (Russian Empire or Soviet Russia); after 1991, Russia and 14 other republics.

sources.says: The Treaty, along with the Declaration of the Creation of the USSR was approved on 30 December 1922
On 26 December 1991, the Soviet Union was formally dissolved and ceased to exist as a sovereign state.
The Treaty, along with the Declaration of the Creation of the USSR was approved on 30 December 1922

title: Saudi Arabia proclaimed
question: Is there a country called Saudi Arabia?
hint: Most of the Arabian Peninsula. Before 1932, maps show Hejaz and Nejd (or just Arabia).

sources.says: Following the amalgamation of the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd, Abdulaziz issued a royal decree on 23 September 1932 naming the new state ... the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
The name of the state was changed to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia by a decree of September 18, 1932.
In 1932, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia was proclaimed.

notes: Sources give the decree as 18 September (State Department) or the proclamation as 23 September 1932; both are September 1932.

title: North Korea
question: Is there a country called North Korea (Democratic People's Republic of Korea)?
hint: The northern half of the Korean peninsula. Before 1948, maps show one Korea (Chosen under Japan until 1945).

sources.says: ...establishment of the Republic of Korea in southern Korea on 15 August 1948, which promptly followed the establishment of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea in northern Korea on 9 September 1948.
The Democratic People's Republic of Korea was established in the North on 9 September 1948.

notes: From 1945 to 1948, maps may show a Soviet/US occupation line at the 38th parallel. Merged duplicates disagreed on dates: 1948-09..null vs 1948-08..null.

title: Jan Mayen becomes Norwegian
question: Is Jan Mayen shown as part of Norway?
hint: A small island in the Arctic Ocean northeast of Iceland, labelled (Nor.). Earlier maps leave it unclaimed.

sources.says: On 27 February 1930, the island was made de jure a part of the Kingdom of Norway.

notes: Formal annexation was 27 February 1930, after the Meteorological Institute's claims of 1922 and 1926.

title: Lake Chad shrinks
question: Is Lake Chad shown as a small southern pool with marsh to the north, rather than one large lake?
hint: Where Chad, Niger, Nigeria and Cameroon meet. Older maps and photos show one big open lake.

sources.says: From June 1966 to January 1973, the area of Lake Chad shrank from 22,772 to 15,400 km2 ..., further shrunk to 4,398 km2 ... in 1975, and only 1,756 km2 ... in February 1994.

Around 1973, the lake was in a phase called "Normal Lake Chad"—a single body of water. ... By 1976, the lake had transitioned to "Small Lake Chad." It had separated into two areas: the northern basin and the southern basin.

notes: The shrinking was gradual, so there is no single legal date. Wikipedia gives the area collapse by 1975 and NASA Landsat shows the lake split by 1976; 1975 is a judgement call within 1973-76. The northern basin has refilled seasonally in wet years. This mostly shows on satellite and physical maps; many political maps still draw the old shoreline.

title: Salton Sea forms
question: Is there a large lake (the Salton Sea) in the desert of southern California?
hint: Southeast of Palm Springs, north of the Mexican border. Before 1905, maps show the dry Salton Sink.

sources.says: The modern lake was formed from an inflow of water from the Colorado River in 1905.
In 1905, the flooding Colorado River breached its banks once again, spilling via the Alamo River and the New River ... The breach was closed in 1907

notes: The lake formed from 1905 and filled until the breach was closed in February 1907, so 1905-1909 maps can also show it.

title: Lake Volta fills
question: Is there a large lake (Lake Volta) filling the middle of Ghana?
hint: Eastern Ghana, behind the Akosombo Dam. Before 1964, maps show the separate White and Black Volta rivers meeting.

sources.says: Lake Volta was formed between 1962 and 1966 and necessitated the relocation of about 80,000 people

With the closure of the Akosombo Dam in May 1964, the riverine condition of the Volta River gradually transformed ... When the water began to rise in 1964, Tongu communities did not return to the Lower Volta

notes: The dam was closed in 1964 (Miescher in Daedalus says May; an FAO graph note says January), so only the year is given. The lake filled over 1964-1968, and the dam was inaugurated on 22 January 1966. Merged duplicates disagreed on dates: 1964..null vs 1965..null.

title: Aral Sea splits in two
question: Is the Aral Sea shown as two or more separate lakes?
hint: On the Kazakhstan-Uzbekistan border, east of the Caspian. Older maps show one large lake.

sources.says: In 1987, the lake split into two separate bodies of water: the North Aral Sea (the Lesser Sea, or Small Aral Sea) and the South Aral Sea (the Greater Sea, or Large Aral Sea).
It split from the South Aral Sea in 1987–1988 as water levels dropped due to river diversion for agriculture.
The North Aral Sea (sometimes called the Small Aral Sea) had separated from the South (Large) Aral Sea.

notes: The 1987 split is the first clear change visible on maps. Wikipedia gives 1987; the North Aral Sea article says 1987-1988.

title: Aral Sea mostly gone
question: Is the Aral Sea shown as a few small remnant lakes with most of its old bed dry?
hint: On the Kazakhstan-Uzbekistan border. Maps from before the 2000s show a large lake, or two big lobes.

sources.says: By 2007, it had declined to 10% of its original size, splitting into four lakes: the North Aral Sea, the eastern and western basins of the once far larger South Aral Sea, and the smaller intermediate Barsakelmes Lake.
Especially large retreats in the eastern lobe of the South Aral Sea appear to have occurred between 2005 and 2009. ... In 2014, the eastern lobe of the South Aral Sea completely disappeared.

notes: The decline was gradual. The southern connection broke in 2001, the biggest retreats came in 2005-09, and the eastern basin first dried completely in 2014 but refills in wet years. 2007 follows Wikipedia's 'largely dried up into desert by 2007'.

title: Constantinople becomes Istanbul
question: Is the city on the Bosphorus labelled Istanbul (rather than Constantinople)?
hint: Where Europe meets Asia. Constantinople on most foreign maps before 1930.

sources.says: The name Constantinople, which remained in use for 1600 years, was officially changed as İstanbul on 28 March 1930
Beginning in 1930, Turkey officially requested that other countries use Turkish names for Turkish cities ... State Department began using "Istanbul" in May 1930.

notes: Often tied to the Turkish Postal Service Law of 28 March 1930 (not confirmed in the cited pages). Merged duplicates disagreed on dates: 1930-03..null vs 1930..null.

title: French West Africa
question: Is most of West Africa one block of French territory (French West Africa)?
hint: From Senegal to Niger. After 1960, maps show separate countries such as Senegal, Mali, Niger and Ivory Coast.

sources.says: The federation existed from 1895 until 1958. Its capital was Saint-Louis in Senegal until 1902, and then Dakar until the federation's collapse in 1960.

Mali Federation became independent on 20 June, then split into Mali and Senegal on 20 August | Dahomey (renamed to Benin in 1975) became independent on 1 August | Niger, independent on 3 August | Upper Volta (renamed to Burkina Faso in 1984), independent on 5 August | Ivory Coast (Côte d'Ivoire), independent on 7 August

notes: The French block grew through the 1880s-1900s; 1895 is when the federation was created, and it was put on a permanent footing in 1904. Legally the federation ended in 1958, but the territories stayed in the French Community until most became independent in June-August 1960 (Guinea in October 1958, Mauritania in November 1960). Merged duplicates disagreed on dates: 1895..1960-08 vs 1895..1958-10.

title: Pakistan created
question: Is there a country called Pakistan?
hint: Northwest of India, with a separate East Pakistan until 1971. Before 1947, maps show British India.

sources.says: On 14 August 1947, the new Dominion of Pakistan came into being, with Muhammad Ali Jinnah sworn in as its first Governor-General in Karachi.
The United States recognized the Dominion of Pakistan as an independent state on August 15, 1947

title: Germany absorbs Austria
question: Is Austria shown as part of Germany?
hint: Central Europe. Germany is unusually large, taking in Austria and, from late 1938, the Sudetenland.

sources.says: ...the annexation of the Federal State of Austria into Nazi Germany on 12 March 1938.
A provisional government in Allied-occupied Austria declared the Anschluss "null und nichtig" (null and void) on 27 April 1945.
...it ended just 12 years later in May 1945, when the Allies defeated Germany and entered Berlin

notes: One, but it's huge' = 1941-45. Austria, the clearest marker, was separate again from 27 April 1945, and the Reich itself ended in May 1945.

title: Two Germanys
question: Is Germany split into two countries, East and West Germany?
hint: Central Europe. Before 1949 there is one Germany (occupation zones in 1945-49); after October 1990 there is one again.

sources.says: West Germany was the common English name for the Federal Republic of Germany (FRG) from its formation on 23 May 1949 until its reunification with East Germany on 3 October 1990.
East Germany, officially the German Democratic Republic (GDR), was a country in Central Europe from its formation on 7 October 1949 until its reunification with West Germany ... on 3 October 1990.

notes: Two German states existed only from 7 October 1949, when the GDR was founded; West Germany dates from 23 May 1949. Reunification was 3 October 1990. Merged duplicates disagreed on dates: 1949-10..1990-10 vs 1949-05..1990-10.

title: Persia renamed Iran
question: Is the country between Iraq and Afghanistan labelled Iran (not Persia)?
hint: Southwest Asia. Before 1935, maps show Persia.

sources.says: The exonym Persia was the official name of Iran in the Western world before March 1935
In 1935, Reza Shah requested that foreign governments refer to the country as 'Iran' rather than 'Persia' in official correspondence.

notes: The request took effect at Nowruz (21 March) 1935. In 1959 'Persia' was allowed again alongside Iran, so a few later maps say 'Iran (Persia)'.

title: Cambodia independent
question: Is Cambodia shown as an independent country (as Cambodia, the Khmer Republic or Kampuchea), not part of French Indochina?
hint: Southeast Asia, between Thailand and Vietnam. Before 1953 it is a protectorate inside French Indochina.

sources.says: Under the reign of King Norodom Sihanouk, Cambodia gained independence from France on 9 November 1953.
Cambodia previously had been part of Indochina as a Protectorate of France and had become an independent state as part of the French Union in 1949.

notes: Full independence came on 9 November 1953; it had been an associated state of the French Union since 1949. The name changed to Khmer Republic (1970-75) and Kampuchea (1976-89), so the question accepts all three names.

title: Italian Eritrea
question: Is Eritrea shown as an Italian colony?
hint: On the Red Sea coast north of Ethiopia. Before 1890 the coast is Ottoman-Egyptian or Ethiopian; later maps show British administration, then Ethiopia.

sources.says: ...Eritrea was officially declared an Italian colony in the royal decree of 1 January 1890
British forces defeated the Italian army in Eritrea in 1941 at the Battle of Keren and placed the colony under British military administration until Allied forces could determine its fate.
Italy lost the colonies of Italian Libya and Italian East Africa. The latter consisted of Italian Ethiopia, Italian Eritrea, and Italian Somaliland.
Infobox: signed 10 February 1947; effective 15 September 1947.

notes: Italy') keeps Eritrea Italian until about 1952, which is wrong. Italy lost control in April 1941 to the British Military Administration and gave up its claim in the 1947 Paris treaty (in force 15 September 1947). The end date uses the legal renunciation; maps from 1941-47 may already show 'British administration'.

title: Eritrea joined to Ethiopia
question: Is Eritrea shown as part of Ethiopia?
hint: Ethiopia reaches the Red Sea coast. Before 1952 Eritrea is Italian or British-run; after 1993 it is independent and Ethiopia is landlocked.

sources.says: ...continuing until the discharge of the federation on 15 September 1952, concurrent with the signing of the Termination of Powers Proclamation.
On 15 November 1962, the Eritrean Assembly voted unanimously to dissolve the federation and incorporate Eritrea into the Ethiopian Empire as a province.
Infobox: De jure independence, 24 May 1993.
The United States recognized the Republic of Eritrea on April 27, 1993, ... on the same date Eritrea declared its independence.

notes: Ethiopia' = 1952-53, which is correct. It was a federation from 1952 and annexed in 1962. Independence was declared on 27 April 1993; Independence Day is 24 May 1993 (used here). Ethiopia had lost control in May 1991.

title: Newfoundland outside Canada
question: Is Newfoundland shown separately from Canada?
hint: The island at the mouth of the Gulf of St Lawrence, with Labrador. From 1949, maps show both inside Canada.

sources.says: On March 31, 1949, it became the tenth and most recent province to join the Canadian Confederation as "Newfoundland".
Newfoundland joined Canada in the final hours of 31 March 1949.

notes: In fact Newfoundland was outside Canada for every map before April 1949: a British colony, then a dominion from 1907.

title: Hot Springs renamed Truth or Consequences
question: Is the town on the Rio Grande in southern New Mexico labelled Truth or Consequences (not Hot Springs)?
hint: On detailed US maps, north of Las Cruces on the Rio Grande. Before 1950 it is Hot Springs.

sources.says: It has frequently been noted on lists of unusual place names for having chosen to rename itself in March 1950 after the Truth or Consequences radio show.
On March 31, 1950, the town officially changed its name to Truth or Consequences.

notes: This small town only appears on detailed US maps, never on world maps or desk globes, so it may not suit the game.

title: United Arab Republic (Egypt and Syria)
question: Are Egypt and Syria shown as one country, the United Arab Republic?
hint: Egypt and Syria share one name and colour even though Israel and Jordan lie between them. Egypt alone kept the UAR name until 1971.

sources.says: The United Arab Republic was established on 1 February 1958 as the first step towards a larger pan-Arab state

notes: The Egypt-Syria union lasted from 1 February 1958 to 28 September 1961. Maps from 1961-71 still label Egypt alone 'United Arab Republic'; this question is about the union, so it answers no for those maps.

title: Two Vietnams
question: Is Vietnam split into North and South Vietnam?
hint: Southeast Asia, divided near the 17th parallel. Before 1954, maps show French Indochina (Tonkin, Annam, Cochinchina); after 1976, one Vietnam.

sources.says: The accords, which were signed on 21 July 1954, set out the following terms in relation to Vietnam
On 2 July 1976, North and South Vietnam were merged to form the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.
The designation North Vietnam became common usage after 1954, when the Geneva Accords provisionally partitioned Vietnam into communist and non-communist zones.
On 2 July 1976, North and South Vietnam were merged to form the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.

notes: Saigon fell in April 1975, but formal reunification was 2 July 1976.

title: Bangladesh independent
question: Is there a country called Bangladesh?
hint: At the head of the Bay of Bengal, east of India. Before 1971 it is East Pakistan (East Bengal before 1955).

sources.says: ...Bangladesh became a sovereign nation on 16 December 1971.
The Pakistan Army's violent crackdown led Awami League leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman to declare independence of East Pakistan as the sovereign state of Bangladesh on 26 March 1971.
Recognition of Bangladeshi Independence, 1972.
Sheikh Mujibur Rahman made a declaration of independence at Dacca on 26 March 1971.

notes: Independence was declared on 26 March 1971, but Pakistan held the territory until it surrendered on 16 December 1971. The span uses December 1971, when the state actually took effect.

title: British Tanganyika Territory
question: Is the land south of Lake Victoria shown as British (Tanganyika Territory)?
hint: East Africa, south of Lake Victoria. Before 1920 it is German East Africa; from December 1961 it is independent Tanganyika.

sources.says: The name was chosen by the British with the Treaty of Versailles, and as such the name took effect when Britain was given control of Tanganyika in 1920.
From 20 July 1922, it was formalised into a League of Nations mandate under British rule.
British rule came to an end on 9 December 1961.

notes: British' = 1960. In fact it was British for every map from 1920 to 1961. British forces had occupied it since 1916; the Treaty of Versailles gave control in 1920, and the mandate was formalised in July 1922.

title: Independent Tanganyika
question: Is there an independent country called Tanganyika?
hint: East Africa, south of Lake Victoria. From 1964 the same land is part of Tanzania.

sources.says: British rule came to an end on 9 December 1961.
The United States recognized Tanganyika on December 9, 1961
...the archipelago merged with mainland Tanganyika on 26 April 1964.

title: Tanzania
question: Is there a country called Tanzania?
hint: East Africa, south of Lake Victoria, including Zanzibar. Before 1964, maps show Tanganyika (and Zanzibar separately).

sources.says: The new country was then named the United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar. ... On 29 October of the same year, the country was renamed the United Republic of Tanzania

notes: The union was formed on 26 April 1964 as the United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar and renamed Tanzania on 29 October 1964.

title: Most of Sinai held by Israel
question: Is most of the Sinai Peninsula shown as held by Israel?
hint: Between Egypt and Israel; look for Israeli colour or 'Israeli-occupied' across the Sinai. Otherwise it is Egyptian.

sources.says: After Central America (then the Captaincy General of Guatemala) declared its independence from the Spanish Empire in September 1821, it was annexed by the First Mexican Empire in January 1822 before regaining its independence and forming a federal republic in 1823.
on July 1, 1823 the Central American provinces formed the Federal Republic of Central America, with only the province of Chiapas choosing to remain a part of Mexico

title: Federal Republic of Central America
question: Is Central America one country (the Federal Republic or United Provinces of Central America)?
hint: One state from Guatemala to Costa Rica; after 1838-41 maps show five republics.

sources.says: The country's initial name, adopted at independence from the First Mexican Empire on 1 July 1823, was the United Provinces of Central America

notes: States seceded from 1838; federal officials left office on 2 February 1839 and Carrera's dissolution decree followed on 17 April 1839. El Salvador held out until 1841. 1839 is used.

title: Chiapas joins Mexico
question: Is Chiapas part of Mexico?
hint: Mexico's southernmost state, bordering Guatemala. Before 1821 it belonged to the Captaincy General of Guatemala; 1823-24 maps may put it in Central America.

sources.says: The State of Chiapas was officially declared in 1824, with its first constitution in 1826.
Mexico annexed Chiapas formally in 1824 and made its first formal claim to the Soconusco in 1825.

notes: The Soconusco district joined Mexico only in 1842; the border with Guatemala was fixed in 1882.

title: Republic of Yucatán
question: Is the Yucatán Peninsula shown as a separate Republic of Yucatán?
hint: South-east Mexico. Briefly independent in the 1840s; otherwise part of Mexico.

sources.says: The second Republic of Yucatán began in 1841, with its declaration of independence from the Centralist Republic of Mexico. ... On March 16, 1841 at the first City Council meeting in Mérida, a crowd ... broke into the room calling for the independence of Yucatán.
The rebellion of the indigenous Maya was put down in August 1848 and August 17 of that year, Barbachano ordered the resumption of a confederation of Mexico

title: Mosquito Coast separate from Nicaragua

sources.says: In 1844, the British government declared a new protectorate over the Mosquito Kingdom

In November 1894 the Mosquito Coast was militarily incorporated into Nicaragua.

notes: The end date is solid, but legal status changed in 1860 (Treaty of Managua), when the area became an autonomous reserve under Nicaraguan suzerainty. Maps of 1860-1894 vary in showing it separately.

title: Costa Rica annexes Guanacaste
question: Is Guanacaste (the Nicoya Peninsula region) part of Costa Rica rather than Nicaragua?

sources.says: After a plebiscite in 1824–25, Costa Rica annexed the territory of Guanacaste.

notes: Costa Rica dates the annexation to 25 July 1824; Nicaragua recognised it in the 1858 Cañas-Jerez treaty.

title: Haiti split into north and south
